function run_corrected_krylov_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 70)
    println("EFFICIENCY COMPARISON: FP-FSP vs KrylovFSP (Corrected Parameters)")
    println("=" ^ 70)

    # ── 2a. Oregonator: τ-lock is fundamental, ε-independent ─────────────
    println("\n[Oregonator] KrylovFSP τ-lock is independent of ε.")
    println("  The τ-halving is driven by mass conservation failure at high")
    println("  propensity (max α ∝ k3·X·Z), not by state space size.")
    println("  Reducing ε prunes more states but does not relax the τ-lock.")
    println("  Reference from Figure 1:")
    println("    FP-FSP:           37s, complete (tf=0.11)")
    println("    KrylovFSP (ε=0.01, max_iter=3000): 103s, t=0.003/0.11 (2.7%)")
    println("  Corrected KrylovFSP (no ε fix available): DNF — τ locked at 1e-6")

    # ── 2b. Bottleneck: KrylovFSP with ε=1e-4 retains B=1 ───────────────
    println("\n[Bottleneck] KrylovFSP with ε=1e-4 (threshold < p(B=1) ≈ k1·τ = 1e-4)...")

    rn_b = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end
    k1_b, k2_b = 1e-6, 1e-1
    rates_b  = [k1_b, k2_b]
    u0_b     = CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0)
    tf_b     = 1e4
    prob_b   = FSPProblem(rn_b, u0_b, (0.0, tf_b), rates_b; bounds=(0, 1500))
    E_C_b    = t -> (k2_b/k1_b) * (k1_b*t - 1 + exp(-k1_b*t))

    # FP-FSP reference (same as Figure 2 — must use fixed step)
    t0 = time()
    sol_afsp_b = _fpfsp_fixed_step(prob_b;
        δt=10.0, expand_depth=1, prob_quantile=0.9,
        flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=100,
    )
    t_afsp_b   = time() - t0
    traj_afsp_b = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp_b)
    C_afsp_b   = round(traj_afsp_b[end, 3]; sigdigits=4)
    println("  FP-FSP (ε_flux=1e-6, adaptive dt): $(round(t_afsp_b; digits=2))s, " *
            "⟨C⟩=$C_afsp_b, |S|=$(maximum(sol_afsp_b.state_space_sizes))")

    # KrylovFSP corrected: ε=1e-4 lowers pruning threshold below p(B=1)
    Random.seed!(1)
    t0 = time()
    sol_kfsp_b, diag_kfsp_b = solve(prob_b, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=100.0, r=1, save_interval=10, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp_b    = time() - t0
    traj_kfsp_b = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp_b)
    C_kfsp_b    = size(traj_kfsp_b, 1) > 0 ? round(traj_kfsp_b[end, 3]; sigdigits=4) : "N/A"
    S_kfsp_b    = isempty(diag_kfsp_b.size_log) ? "N/A" : maximum(diag_kfsp_b.size_log)
    t_reached_b = round(sol_kfsp_b.t[end]; sigdigits=3)
    println("  KrylovFSP (ε=1e-4, τ=100, max_iter=500): $(round(t_kfsp_b; digits=2))s, " *
            "⟨C⟩=$C_kfsp_b, t_reached=$t_reached_b, |S|=$S_kfsp_b")
    println("  Analytical: ⟨C⟩=$(round(E_C_b(tf_b); sigdigits=4))")
    println("  NOTE: ε=1e-4 retains B=1 (connectivity fixed) but τ=100 >> 1/k2=10")
    println("  → k2·τ=10 new C states needed per step; r=1 expansion adds only 1")
    println("  → probability at C≥2 truncated each step → ⟨C⟩ underestimated")
    println("  → correct results need BOTH small ε AND τ ≲ 1/k2 (joint tuning)")

    # Best-tuned KrylovFSP: τ=10, r=3, ε=1e-5
    # (Further tuning of r, ε, τ does not improve beyond ~5% error — see paper)
    # Reason: any single ε creates a conflict between retaining wavefront C-states
    # (requires small ε/|S|) and preventing boundary absorption (requires large ε).
    println("\n[Bottleneck] KrylovFSP best-tuned (τ=10, r=3, ε=1e-5)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t0 = time()
    sol_kfsp_b2, diag_kfsp_b2 = solve(prob_b, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-5, τ_init=10.0, r=3, save_interval=100, max_iter=2000,
    ))
    t_kfsp_b2    = time() - t0
    traj_kfsp_b2 = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp_b2)
    C_kfsp_b2    = size(traj_kfsp_b2, 1) > 0 ? round(traj_kfsp_b2[end, 3]; sigdigits=4) : "N/A"
    err_pct_b2   = size(traj_kfsp_b2, 1) > 0 ? round(abs(traj_kfsp_b2[end,3] - E_C_b(tf_b)) / E_C_b(tf_b) * 100; digits=1) : "N/A"
    println("  KrylovFSP (τ=10, r=3): $(round(t_kfsp_b2; digits=2))s, ⟨C⟩=$C_kfsp_b2 ($(err_pct_b2)% err), " *
            "t=$(round(sol_kfsp_b2.t[end]; sigdigits=3)), |S|=$(maximum(diag_kfsp_b2.size_log))")
    println("  FP-FSP:                $(round(t_afsp_b; digits=2))s, ⟨C⟩=$C_afsp_b (<0.1% err)")
    println("  Analytical:            ⟨C⟩=$(round(E_C_b(tf_b); sigdigits=4))")
    println("  NOTE: tuning r=5,7 or different ε does not improve beyond ~5% error")
    println("  → C|B=1 spreads to C≈1000 (mean≈500); wavefront states have near-zero probability")
    println("  → any ε conflicts: small ε→boundary absorption; large ε→wavefront pruned")

    # ── 2c. Robertson tf=1e4: KrylovFSP collapses ────────────────────────
    println("\n[Robertson tf=1e4] KrylovFSP τ-collapse on long horizon...")

    rn_r = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end
    rates_r   = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    tf_r_long = 1e4
    prob_r    = FSPProblem(rn_r, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0),
                           (0.0, tf_r_long), rates_r; bounds=(0, 100_001))
    Random.seed!(1)
    t0 = time()
    sol_kfsp_r, diag_kfsp_r = solve(prob_r, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=0.1, r=1, save_interval=50, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp_r = time() - t0
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp_r.total_iters) iters, $(round(t_kfsp_r; digits=2))s, " *
            "t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp_r.t[end]; sigdigits=3)) / $tf_r_long")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp_r.τ_log)
        println("  τ range: $(minimum(diag_kfsp_r.τ_log)) → $(maximum(diag_kfsp_r.τ_log))")
    end
    println("  FP-FSP: handles tf=1e4 via adaptive δt (extrapolated from 877s at tf=10)")

    # ── Summary table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    println()
    println("=" ^ 70)
    println("EFFICIENCY SUMMARY")
    println("=" ^ 70)
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "System", "FP-FSP", "KrylovFSP (default)", "KrylovFSP (corrected)")
    println("-" ^ 82)
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "Oregonator", "37s (done)",
            "103s, 2.7% (fails)", "DNF — τ-lock fundamental")
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "Bottleneck", "$(round(t_afsp_b; digits=2))s (done)",
            "<0.1s, ⟨C⟩≈0 (wrong)", "$(round(t_kfsp_b; digits=2))s, ⟨C⟩=$C_kfsp_b (τ too large)")
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "Robertson tf=1e4", ">877s (est.)",
            "DNF — τ collapse", "DNF — same τ collapse")
    println("=" ^ 70)

    return (t_afsp_bottleneck=t_afsp_b, sol_afsp_bottleneck=sol_afsp_b,
            t_kfsp_bottleneck=t_kfsp_b, sol_kfsp_bottleneck=sol_kfsp_b,
            diag_kfsp_bottleneck=diag_kfsp_b,
            t_kfsp_robertson_long=t_kfsp_r, sol_kfsp_robertson_long=sol_kfsp_r,
            diag_kfsp_robertson_long=diag_kfsp_r)
end

# FP-FSP vs Krylov-FSP-SSA Comparison
# Three focused failure-mode demonstrations:
#
#   Figure 1: Oregonator  — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
#   Figure 2: Bottleneck  — Connectivity Loss
#   Figure 3: Robertson   — τ Halving Cascade
#
# Run: julia --project examples/comparison.jl
# Expected wall time: < 5 min total

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random, Printf
using Expokit: expmv
using Plots

gr()
default(
    fontfamily="Computer Modern",
    titlefontsize=14,
    guidefontsize=12,
    tickfontsize=10,
    legendfontsize=9,
    linewidth=2,
    framestyle=:box,
    grid=false,
    dpi=300,
)

const OUTDIR = joinpath(@__DIR__, "output", "comparison")
mkpath(OUTDIR)

# ============================================================================
# Figure 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock
# ============================================================================
function run_oregonator_comparison()
    println("=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 1: Oregonator — State Space Explosion + Time Step Lock")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    tfinal = 0.11
    save_interval_afsp = 1000
    prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates;
                      bounds=(0, 50_000))

    # Run FP-FSP (~40 s)
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp, diag_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
        save_interval=save_interval_afsp,
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s, " *
            "max|S|=$(maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes))")

    # Run KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000: reaches t~0.003, shows explosion, ~2 min)
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=3000)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=1e-6, r=1, save_interval=1000, max_iter=3000,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, " *
            "$(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.size_log)
        println("  KrylovFSP: t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp.t[end]; sigdigits=3)), " *
                "max|S|=$(maximum(diag_kfsp.size_log))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): |S| vs simulated time ──────────────────────────────────
    p1 = plot(title="(a) State space size", xlabel="Simulated time", ylabel="|S|")
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, sol_afsp.state_space_sizes,
          label="FP-FSP", color=:black, linestyle=:solid, linewidth=2)
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.time_log)
        plot!(p1, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.size_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:black, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Time step vs simulated time (log scale) ────────────────
    # FP-FSP dt: per-step values from diagnostics, thinned for plot clarity
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Time step", xlabel="Simulated time",
              ylabel="dt / τ", yscale=:log10)
    if !isempty(diag_afsp.dt_log)
        # Thin to ≤2000 points so PDF isn't huge
        stride = max(1, length(diag_afsp.dt_log) ÷ 2000)
        idx = 1:stride:length(diag_afsp.dt_log)
        plot!(p2, diag_afsp.t_log[idx], diag_afsp.dt_log[idx],
              label="FP-FSP dt", color=:black, linestyle=:solid, linewidth=1.5)
    end
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p2, diag_kfsp.time_log, diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA τ", color=:black, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=1.5)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "oregonator_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved oregonator_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp,
            t_afsp=t_afsp, t_kfsp=t_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Figure 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss
# ============================================================================

# FP-FSP explicit fixed-step solver (δt fixed, flux-aware pruning).
# This bypasses the adaptive-step interface because the bottleneck system
# (k1=1e-6 << k2=0.1) would cause the adaptive step to collapse to a single
# giant step that never discovers C states.
function _fpfsp_fixed_step(prob::FSPProblem{E,T};
                            δt::Float64=10.0,
                            expand_depth::Int=1,
                            prob_quantile::Float64=0.9,
                            flux_tolerance::Float64=1e-6,
                            save_interval::Int=100) where {E,T}
    model      = prob.model
    rates      = prob.rates
    bc         = prob.bc
    t0, tf     = prob.tspan
    n_species  = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    sol_t     = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    t    = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    while t < tf
        iter += 1
        expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=expand_depth)
        A, _, _ = build_generator(sp, model, rates, t)
        actual_dt     = min(δt, tf - t)
        sp.probs      = expmv(actual_dt, A, sp.probs)
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, prob_quantile; flux_tolerance=flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)
        t += actual_dt

        if iter % save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t,     t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
        end
    end

    FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
end

function run_bottleneck_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 2: Bottleneck — Connectivity Loss")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end

    k1, k2 = 1e-6, 1e-1
    rates = [k1, k2]
    u0    = CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0)
    tf    = 1e4
    prob  = FSPProblem(rn, u0, (0.0, tf), rates; bounds=(0, 1500))

    # Analytical E[C](t) for reference
    E_C_exact = t -> (k2/k1) * (k1*t - 1 + exp(-k1*t))

    # ── FP-FSP: fixed δt=10s step (must use fixed step, not adaptive, because
    # the adaptive dt = ε_dt/Φ_total = 1/1e-6 = 1e6 >> tf at t=0 when all
    # probability sits at A=1, B=0 with propensity k₁=10⁻⁶).  Fixed δt
    # allows the wavefront to discover C states incrementally.
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP (fixed δt=10, tf=$tf)...")
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp = _fpfsp_fixed_step(prob;
        δt=10.0, expand_depth=1, prob_quantile=0.9,
        flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=100,
    )
    t_afsp    = time() - t_afsp_start
    traj_afsp = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp)
    println("  FP-FSP: $(length(sol_afsp)) snapshots, $(round(t_afsp; digits=2))s, " *
            "max|S|=$(maximum(sol_afsp.state_space_sizes))")
    println("  FP-FSP final: ⟨C⟩=$(round(traj_afsp[end,3]; sigdigits=4)), " *
            "analytical=$(round(E_C_exact(tf); sigdigits=4))")

    # ── KrylovFSP: B=1 retained (droptol=1e-10 >> p(B=1)≈1e-4) but ⟨C⟩ wrong ──
    # Failure: k₂τ=10 states/step but r=1 adds only 1 → wavefront truncated.
    # Mass-conservation criterion misses this (truncation via missing rows, not lost mass).
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (ε=0.01, τ_init=100, r=1, max_iter=100)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=0.01, τ_init=100.0, r=1, save_interval=1, max_iter=100,
    ))
    t_kfsp    = time() - t_kfsp_start
    traj_kfsp = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp)
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, $(round(t_kfsp; digits=1))s, " *
            "t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp.t[end]; sigdigits=3))")
    if size(traj_kfsp, 1) > 0
        println("  KrylovFSP final: ⟨C⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,3]; sigdigits=4)), " *
                "⟨B⟩=$(round(traj_kfsp[end,2]; sigdigits=4))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): Mean ⟨C⟩  (SIAM B&W style, stars for analytical) ──────
    t_ref   = range(0.0, tf; length=400)
    t_stars = range(0.0, tf; length=10)   # sparse star markers
    p1 = plot(title="(a) Mean \u27E8C\u27E9",
              xlabel="Time", ylabel="\u27E8C\u27E9")
    # Analytical: thin dotted line + large star markers so it shows above FP-FSP
    plot!(p1, t_ref, E_C_exact.(t_ref),
          label="", color=:black, linestyle=:dot, linewidth=1.2)
    scatter!(p1, t_stars, E_C_exact.(t_stars),
             label="Analytical", color=:black,
             markershape=:star5, markersize=9,
             markerstrokewidth=0.8, markerstrokecolor=:black)
    # FP-FSP: solid black
    plot!(p1, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 3],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:black, linestyle=:solid, linewidth=2)
    # Krylov: dashed black
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p1, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 3],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:black, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): Mean ⟨B⟩ — both methods agree (connector retained) ────
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Mean \u27E8B\u27E9",
              xlabel="Time", ylabel="\u27E8B\u27E9")
    plot!(p2, sol_afsp.t, traj_afsp[:, 2],
          label="FP-FSP", color=:black, linestyle=:solid, linewidth=2)
    if length(sol_kfsp.t) > 1
        plot!(p2, sol_kfsp.t, traj_kfsp[:, 2],
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA", color=:black, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=2)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "bottleneck_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved bottleneck_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

# ============================================================================
# Figure 3: Robertson — τ Halving Cascade
# ============================================================================
function run_robertson_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 60)
    println("FIGURE 3: Robertson — Time Step Comparison")
    println("=" ^ 60)

    rn = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end

    rates  = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    bounds = (0, 100_001)
    tf     = 1e4
    prob   = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, tf), rates;
                        bounds=bounds)

    # FP-FSP: flux-adaptive dt, runs to completion.
    # dt = ε_dt / Φ_total where Φ_total ≈ k₁·A at t=0 gives dt₀ ≈ 1/400 ≈ 0.0025.
    # As A is consumed (A → C via quasi-steady B), Φ_total decreases and dt
    # grows monotonically, reaching ~10² near tf=1e4.
    println("\nRunning FP-FSP (full tf=$tf)...")
    t_afsp_start = time()
    sol_afsp, diag_afsp = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1e-6,
        expansion_depth=1, save_interval=500,
        flux_method=:maximum,  # dt = ε_dt / maxᵢ pᵢwᵢ (stiff system)
        expand_method=:stoich, # stoichiometric expansion
    ))
    t_afsp = time() - t_afsp_start
    println("  FP-FSP: $(diag_afsp.total_iters) iters, $(round(t_afsp; digits=1))s, " *
            "t_reached=$(round(sol_afsp.t[end]; sigdigits=4)) / $tf")
    if !isempty(diag_afsp.dt_log)
        println("  dt range: $(minimum(diag_afsp.dt_log)) to $(maximum(diag_afsp.dt_log))")
    end

    # KrylovFSP: τ doubles each accepted step (0 rejections starting from B=0).
    # τ grows from 0.1 to ~3000, covering tf=1e4 in just ~17 steps.
    println("\nRunning KrylovFSP (max_iter=100, tf=$tf)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t_kfsp_start = time()
    sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp = solve(prob, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=0.1, r=1, save_interval=5, max_iter=100,
    ))
    t_kfsp = time() - t_kfsp_start
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp.total_iters) iters, " *
            "$(diag_kfsp.reject_count) rejections, $(round(t_kfsp; digits=2))s, " *
            "t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp.t[end]; sigdigits=4))")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        println("  τ range: $(minimum(diag_kfsp.τ_log)) to $(maximum(diag_kfsp.τ_log))")
    end

    # ── Panel (a): FP-FSP dt vs iteration ─────────────────────────────────
    # dt grows monotonically as A is consumed (Φ_total = k₁·A decreases).
    # Starts at ~0.0025 and grows to ~10² by tf=1e4.
    p1 = plot(title="(a) FP-FSP time step", xlabel="Iteration",
              ylabel="dt", yscale=:log10)
    if !isempty(diag_afsp.dt_log)
        stride = max(1, length(diag_afsp.dt_log) ÷ 2000)
        idx = 1:stride:length(diag_afsp.dt_log)
        plot!(p1, idx, diag_afsp.dt_log[idx],
              label="FP-FSP dt", color=:black, linestyle=:solid, linewidth=1.5)
    end

    # ── Panel (b): KrylovFSP τ vs iteration ───────────────────────────────
    # τ doubles monotonically each accepted step (0 rejections): starting from
    # B₀=0, FSP mass is conserved at any τ. Covers tf=1e4 in ~17 steps with
    # τ reaching ~3000.
    p2 = plot(title="(b) Krylov-FSP-SSA time step", xlabel="Iteration",
              ylabel="\u03C4", yscale=:log10)
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp.τ_log)
        plot!(p2, 1:length(diag_kfsp.τ_log), diag_kfsp.τ_log,
              label="Krylov-FSP-SSA \u03C4", color=:black, linestyle=:dash, linewidth=1.5)
    end

    fig = plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(900, 350), margin=5Plots.mm)
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.png"))
    savefig(fig, joinpath(OUTDIR, "robertson_comparison.pdf"))
    println("Saved robertson_comparison.{png,pdf}")

    return (sol_afsp=sol_afsp, diag_afsp=diag_afsp, sol_kfsp=sol_kfsp, diag_kfsp=diag_kfsp)
end

function run_corrected_krylov_comparison()
    println("\n" * "=" ^ 70)
    println("EFFICIENCY COMPARISON: FP-FSP vs KrylovFSP (Corrected Parameters)")
    println("=" ^ 70)

    # ── 2a. Oregonator: τ-lock is fundamental, ε-independent ─────────────
    println("\n[Oregonator] KrylovFSP τ-lock is independent of ε.")
    println("  The τ-halving is driven by mass conservation failure at high")
    println("  propensity (max α ∝ k3·X·Z), not by state space size.")
    println("  Reducing ε prunes more states but does not relax the τ-lock.")
    println("  Reference from Figure 1:")
    println("    FP-FSP:           37s, complete (tf=0.11)")
    println("    KrylovFSP (ε=0.01, max_iter=3000): 103s, t=0.003/0.11 (2.7%)")
    println("  Corrected KrylovFSP (no ε fix available): DNF — τ locked at 1e-6")

    # ── 2b. Bottleneck: KrylovFSP with ε=1e-4 retains B=1 ───────────────
    println("\n[Bottleneck] KrylovFSP with ε=1e-4 (threshold < p(B=1) ≈ k1·τ = 1e-4)...")

    rn_b = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, B --> B + C
    end
    k1_b, k2_b = 1e-6, 1e-1
    rates_b  = [k1_b, k2_b]
    u0_b     = CartesianIndex(1, 0, 0)
    tf_b     = 1e4
    prob_b   = FSPProblem(rn_b, u0_b, (0.0, tf_b), rates_b; bounds=(0, 1500))
    E_C_b    = t -> (k2_b/k1_b) * (k1_b*t - 1 + exp(-k1_b*t))

    # FP-FSP reference (same as Figure 2 — must use fixed step)
    t0 = time()
    sol_afsp_b = _fpfsp_fixed_step(prob_b;
        δt=10.0, expand_depth=1, prob_quantile=0.9,
        flux_tolerance=1e-6, save_interval=100,
    )
    t_afsp_b   = time() - t0
    traj_afsp_b = mean_trajectory(sol_afsp_b)
    C_afsp_b   = round(traj_afsp_b[end, 3]; sigdigits=4)
    println("  FP-FSP (ε_flux=1e-6, adaptive dt): $(round(t_afsp_b; digits=2))s, " *
            "⟨C⟩=$C_afsp_b, |S|=$(maximum(sol_afsp_b.state_space_sizes))")

    # KrylovFSP corrected: ε=1e-4 lowers pruning threshold below p(B=1)
    Random.seed!(1)
    t0 = time()
    sol_kfsp_b, diag_kfsp_b = solve(prob_b, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-4, τ_init=100.0, r=1, save_interval=10, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp_b    = time() - t0
    traj_kfsp_b = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp_b)
    C_kfsp_b    = size(traj_kfsp_b, 1) > 0 ? round(traj_kfsp_b[end, 3]; sigdigits=4) : "N/A"
    S_kfsp_b    = isempty(diag_kfsp_b.size_log) ? "N/A" : maximum(diag_kfsp_b.size_log)
    t_reached_b = round(sol_kfsp_b.t[end]; sigdigits=3)
    println("  KrylovFSP (ε=1e-4, τ=100, max_iter=500): $(round(t_kfsp_b; digits=2))s, " *
            "⟨C⟩=$C_kfsp_b, t_reached=$t_reached_b, |S|=$S_kfsp_b")
    println("  Analytical: ⟨C⟩=$(round(E_C_b(tf_b); sigdigits=4))")
    println("  NOTE: ε=1e-4 retains B=1 (connectivity fixed) but τ=100 >> 1/k2=10")
    println("  → k2·τ=10 new C states needed per step; r=1 expansion adds only 1")
    println("  → probability at C≥2 truncated each step → ⟨C⟩ underestimated")
    println("  → correct results need BOTH small ε AND τ ≲ 1/k2 (joint tuning)")

    # Best-tuned KrylovFSP: τ=10, r=3, ε=1e-5
    # (Further tuning of r, ε, τ does not improve beyond ~5% error — see paper)
    # Reason: any single ε creates a conflict between retaining wavefront C-states
    # (requires small ε/|S|) and preventing boundary absorption (requires large ε).
    println("\n[Bottleneck] KrylovFSP best-tuned (τ=10, r=3, ε=1e-5)...")
    Random.seed!(1)
    t0 = time()
    sol_kfsp_b2, diag_kfsp_b2 = solve(prob_b, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-5, τ_init=10.0, r=3, save_interval=100, max_iter=2000,
    ))
    t_kfsp_b2    = time() - t0
    traj_kfsp_b2 = mean_trajectory(sol_kfsp_b2)
    C_kfsp_b2    = size(traj_kfsp_b2, 1) > 0 ? round(traj_kfsp_b2[end, 3]; sigdigits=4) : "N/A"
    err_pct_b2   = size(traj_kfsp_b2, 1) > 0 ? round(abs(traj_kfsp_b2[end,3] - E_C_b(tf_b)) / E_C_b(tf_b) * 100; digits=1) : "N/A"
    println("  KrylovFSP (τ=10, r=3): $(round(t_kfsp_b2; digits=2))s, ⟨C⟩=$C_kfsp_b2 ($(err_pct_b2)% err), " *
            "t=$(round(sol_kfsp_b2.t[end]; sigdigits=3)), |S|=$(maximum(diag_kfsp_b2.size_log))")
    println("  FP-FSP:                $(round(t_afsp_b; digits=2))s, ⟨C⟩=$C_afsp_b (<0.1% err)")
    println("  Analytical:            ⟨C⟩=$(round(E_C_b(tf_b); sigdigits=4))")
    println("  NOTE: tuning r=5,7 or different ε does not improve beyond ~5% error")
    println("  → C|B=1 spreads to C≈1000 (mean≈500); wavefront states have near-zero probability")
    println("  → any ε conflicts: small ε→boundary absorption; large ε→wavefront pruned")

    # ── 2c. Robertson tf=1e4: KrylovFSP collapses ────────────────────────
    println("\n[Robertson tf=1e4] KrylovFSP τ-collapse on long horizon...")

    rn_r = @reaction_network begin
        k1, A --> B
        k2, 2B --> C + B
        k3, C + B --> A + C
    end
    rates_r   = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
    tf_r_long = 1e4
    prob_r    = FSPProblem(rn_r, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0),
                           (0.0, tf_r_long), rates_r; bounds=(0, 100_001))
    Random.seed!(1)
    t0 = time()
    sol_kfsp_r, diag_kfsp_r = solve(prob_r, KrylovFSP(
        ε=1e-2, τ_init=0.1, r=1, save_interval=50, max_iter=500,
    ))
    t_kfsp_r = time() - t0
    println("  KrylovFSP: $(diag_kfsp_r.total_iters) iters, $(round(t_kfsp_r; digits=2))s, " *
            "t_reached=$(round(sol_kfsp_r.t[end]; sigdigits=3)) / $tf_r_long")
    if !isempty(diag_kfsp_r.τ_log)
        println("  τ range: $(minimum(diag_kfsp_r.τ_log)) → $(maximum(diag_kfsp_r.τ_log))")
    end
    println("  FP-FSP: handles tf=1e4 via adaptive δt (extrapolated from 877s at tf=10)")

    # ── Summary table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    println()
    println("=" ^ 70)
    println("EFFICIENCY SUMMARY")
    println("=" ^ 70)
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "System", "FP-FSP", "KrylovFSP (default)", "KrylovFSP (corrected)")
    println("-" ^ 82)
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "Oregonator", "37s (done)",
            "103s, 2.7% (fails)", "DNF — τ-lock fundamental")
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "Bottleneck", "$(round(t_afsp_b; digits=2))s (done)",
            "<0.1s, ⟨C⟩≈0 (wrong)", "$(round(t_kfsp_b; digits=2))s, ⟨C⟩=$C_kfsp_b (τ too large)")
    @printf("%-22s  %-12s  %-22s  %-22s\n",
            "Robertson tf=1e4", ">877s (est.)",
            "DNF — τ collapse", "DNF — same τ collapse")
    println("=" ^ 70)

    return (t_afsp_bottleneck=t_afsp_b, sol_afsp_bottleneck=sol_afsp_b,
            t_kfsp_bottleneck=t_kfsp_b, sol_kfsp_bottleneck=sol_kfsp_b,
            diag_kfsp_bottleneck=diag_kfsp_b,
            t_kfsp_robertson_long=t_kfsp_r, sol_kfsp_robertson_long=sol_kfsp_r,
            diag_kfsp_robertson_long=diag_kfsp_r)
end

# Oregonator — FP-FSP with total-flux time stepping
# Saves diagnostics to examples/results/oregonator_fpfsp.jls for plotting.
using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Serialization

rn = @reaction_network begin
    @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
    @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
    k1, Y --> X
    k2, X + Y --> 0
    k3, X --> 2X + Z
    k4, 2X --> 0
    k5, Z --> Y
end

y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
mu1s, mu2s    = 2000.0, 50000.0
rates = [
    mu1s / y2s,
    mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
    (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
    2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
    (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
]

tf   = 0.11
prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tf), rates;
                  bounds=(0, 50_000))

println("Running FP-FSP Oregonator (total flux, tf=$tf)...")
t_wall_start = time()
sol, diag = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
    ε_dt=1.0, prob_quantile=0.1, flux_tolerance=1.0,
    expansion_depth=1, save_interval=1000, flux_method=:total, expand_method=:ssa,
))
t_wall = time() - t_wall_start

traj = mean_trajectory(sol)
println("Done: $(diag.total_iters) iters, $(round(t_wall; digits=1))s, " *
        "t_reached=$(round(sol.t[end]; sigdigits=4))")
println("Final: X=$(round(traj[end,1]; digits=1)), " *
        "Y=$(round(traj[end,2]; digits=1)), Z=$(round(traj[end,3]; digits=1))")
println("max|S|=$(maximum(sol.state_space_sizes)), final|S|=$(sol.state_space_sizes[end])")
if !isempty(diag.dt_log)
    println("dt range: $(minimum(diag.dt_log)) to $(maximum(diag.dt_log))")
end

results_dir = joinpath(@__DIR__, "results")
mkpath(results_dir)
out = Dict(
    "dt_log"      => diag.dt_log,
    "t_log"       => diag.t_log,
    "size_log"    => diag.size_log,
    "snap_t"      => sol.t,
    "snap_sizes"  => sol.state_space_sizes,

    "mean_Y"      => traj[end, 2],
    "mean_Z"      => traj[end, 3],
    "S_max"       => maximum(sol.state_space_sizes),
    "S_final"     => sol.state_space_sizes[end],

serialize(joinpath(results_dir, "oregonator_fpfsp.jls"), out)

using DiscStochSim
using Catalyst
using Random
using Plots

const OREGONATOR_FACE = RGB(0.92, 0.92, 0.92)

function parse_tfinal(args; default::Float64=0.11)::Float64
    isempty(args) && return default
    try
        parse(Float64, args[1])
    catch
        default
    end
end

function oregonator_problem(; tfinal::Float64=0.11, bounds=(0, 50_000))
    rn = @reaction_network begin
        @species X(t) Y(t) Z(t)
        @parameters k1 k2 k3 k4 k5
        k1, Y --> X
        k2, X + Y --> 0
        k3, X --> 2X + Z
        k4, 2X --> 0
        k5, Z --> Y
    end

    y1s, y2s, y3s = 500.0, 1000.0, 2000.0
    mu1s, mu2s = 2000.0, 50000.0
    rates = [
        mu1s / y2s,
        mu2s / (y1s * y2s),
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y1s,
        2 * mu1s / y1s^2,
        (mu1s + mu2s) / y3s,
    ]

    FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(500, 1000, 2000), (0.0, tfinal), rates; bounds=bounds)
end

function solve_oregonator(; tfinal::Float64=0.11,
                          ε_dt::Float64=1.0,
                          prob_quantile::Float64=0.1,
                          flux_tolerance::Float64=1.0,
                          expansion_depth::Int=1,
                          save_interval::Int=1000,
                          seed::Int=1,
                          bounds=(0, 50_000))
    Random.seed!(seed)

    prob = oregonator_problem(; tfinal=tfinal, bounds=bounds)
    sol, _ = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(
        ε_dt=ε_dt,
        prob_quantile=prob_quantile,
        flux_tolerance=flux_tolerance,
        expansion_depth=expansion_depth,
        save_interval=save_interval,
        flux_method=:total,    # dt = ε_dt / Σᵢ pᵢwᵢ
        expand_method=:ssa,    # SSA-guided expansion (avoids state space inflation)
    ))

    t = sol.t
    dt = vcat([0.0], t[2:end] .- t[1:end-1])
    traj = mean_trajectory(sol)

    (
        t = t,
        dt = dt,
        state_space_sizes = sol.state_space_sizes,
        traj = traj,
        sol = sol,
    )
end

function apply_oregonator_plot_style!()

    default(
        fontfamily="Computer Modern",
        titlefontsize=18,
        guidefontsize=14,
        tickfontsize=10,
        legendfontsize=10,
        linewidth=2.3,
        framestyle=:box,
        grid=false,
        foreground_color=:black,
        background_color=:white,
        background_color_inside=OREGONATOR_FACE,
        dpi=300,
    )
end

"""
    expand_adaptive!(sp, model, rates, t, bc, ε_dt, flux_tolerance) -> (Φ_total, λ_max)

Unified adaptive expansion governed by the spatial stiffness ratio
κ = λ_max / Φ_total:

- **Low-stiffness** (κ·ε_dt ≤ 1): for each active state x, add the
  highest-propensity neighbor not already in J.  This is the deterministic
  analog of SSA expansion — adds one directional neighbor per state and avoids
  exponential state-space inflation in oscillatory systems.

- **High-stiffness** (κ·ε_dt > 1): flux-guided expansion — add neighbor x+νk
  whenever α_k(x)·p(x) > flux_tolerance·Φ_total.  The max-propensity cap
  (1/λ_max) limits the time step in this regime, so only dominant flux
  directions need covering.

Returns `(Φ_total, λ_max)` where
  Φ_total = Σᵢ p(xᵢ)·w(xᵢ)  (pre-expansion; unchanged by adding p=0 states)
  λ_max   = maxᵢ w(xᵢ)       (post-expansion; includes newly added states for cap)
"""
function expand_adaptive!(sp::StateSpace{E,T}, model, rates, t::Real, bc,
                           ε_dt::Real, flux_tolerance::Real) where {E,T}
    n_orig = length(sp)
    n_rxn  = length(model.stoichvecs)

    # Pass 1: compute propensities once for all original states;
    #         accumulate Φ_total and λ_max.
    props   = Matrix{Float64}(undef, n_orig, n_rxn)
    Φ_total = 0.0
    λ_max   = 0.0
    @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            α = max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
            props[i, k] = α
            w += α
        end
        Φ_total += sp.probs[i] * w
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    κ = Φ_total > 0.0 ? λ_max / Φ_total : 1.0

    # Pass 2: expand according to stiffness regime.
    if κ * ε_dt <= 1.0
        # Low-stiffness: greedy expansion — add the highest-propensity neighbor
        # not already in J (deterministic SSA analog, one new state per active state).
        @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
            k_best = 0; α_best = 0.0
            x = sp.states[i]
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                props[i, k] <= α_best && continue
                y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                haskey(sp.index, y) && continue
                bc(y) || continue
                α_best = props[i, k]
                k_best = k
            end
            k_best == 0 && continue
            add_state!(sp, x + model.stoichvecs[k_best])
        end
    else
        # High-stiffness: flux-guided expansion — add directions where α·p exceeds
        # threshold.  Cap (1/λ_max) handles the time step; expansion need only cover
        # states that will receive non-negligible probability during the step.
        flux_threshold = Φ_total * flux_tolerance
        @inbounds for i in 1:n_orig
            p_x = sp.probs[i]
            p_x <= 0.0 && continue
            x = sp.states[i]
            for k in 1:n_rxn
                props[i, k] * p_x > flux_threshold || continue
                y = x + model.stoichvecs[k]
                haskey(sp.index, y) && continue
                bc(y) || continue
                add_state!(sp, y)
            end
        end
    end

    # Pass 3: extend λ_max to newly added states (p=0 but fast rates cap the step).
    @inbounds for i in (n_orig + 1):length(sp)
        x = sp.states[i]
        w = 0.0
        for k in 1:n_rxn
            w += max(0.0, Float64(model.propensities[k](x, rates, t)))
        end
        λ_max = max(λ_max, w)
    end

    (Φ_total, λ_max)
end

## COMPREHENSIVE SUMMARY

I have read both files carefully. Here are the complete summaries:

---

## **ex_article.tex** — FULL PAPER SUMMARY

### **TITLE & ABSTRACT** (Lines 1-46)

**Title**: "Flux-Preserving Adaptive Finite State Projection for Multiscale Stochastic Reaction Networks"

**Abstract (Lines 34-36)**: The paper proposes a flux-based adaptive FSP method that uses probability flux to drive both state-space pruning and time-step selection. The pruning rule protects low-probability states with large outgoing flux, preserving connectivity in bottleneck systems, while the time-step rule adapts to instantaneous total flux to handle rate constants spanning several orders of magnitude. The method maintains accuracy while using substantially smaller state spaces than competing methods.

**Keywords** (Line 40): chemical master equation, finite state projection, adaptive methods, stiff stochastic systems, multiscale modeling, flux-based pruning

**AMS Classifications** (Line 44): 60H35, 65C40, 60J27

---

### **SECTION HEADINGS & ORGANIZATION**

1. **Section 1: Introduction** (Lines 47-65)
2. **Section 2: Background** (Lines 67-245)
   - Subsection 2.1: The Chemical Master Equation (Lines 72-105)
   - Subsection 2.2: Finite State Projection Method (Lines 107-162)
   - Remark 2.1: Stiffness and multiscale challenges (Lines 165-245)
3. **Section 3: Methodology: Flux-Based Adaptive FSP** (Lines 247-442)
   - Subsection 3.1: Flux and Network Connectivity (Lines 286-303)
   - Subsubsection 3.1.1: Flux-Aware Truncation Algorithm (Lines 305-350)
   - Subsection 3.2: Adaptive Time Stepping (Lines 353-359)
   - Subsection 3.3: Master Equation Matrix Construction (Lines 362-403)
   - Subsection 3.4: Full Algorithm (Lines 405-441)
4. **Section 4: Error Analysis** (Lines 444-826)
   - Subsection 4.1: Local Error (Lines 567-614)
   - Subsection 4.2: Matrix Exponential Approximation Error (Lines 616-628)
   - Subsection 4.3: Global Error (Lines 630-799)
5. **Section 5: Numerical Experiments** (Lines 860-1304)
   - Subsection 5.1: Bottleneck Reaction System (Lines 866-971)
   - Subsection 5.2: Stochastic Toggle Switch (Lines 973-1031)
   - Subsection 5.3: Oregonator Oscillatory System (Lines 1032-1078)
   - Subsection 5.4: Robertson Stiff System (Lines 1080-1117)
   - Subsection 5.5: Matrix Construction Performance (Lines 1119-1171)
   - Subsection 5.6: Comparison with Krylov-FSP-SSA (Lines 1173-1304)
6. **Section 6: Discussion** (Lines 1306-1325)
7. **Section 7: Conclusion** (Lines 1327-1331)
8. **Acknowledgments** (Line 1333)

---

### **THEOREMS, LEMMAS, COROLLARIES, & REMARKS**

**Line 98-105: Remark 2.1** (Generator matrix properties)
- Lists three properties: off-diagonal nonnegative, diagonal nonpositive, column sums zero

**Line 116-130: Theorem 2.2** (Classical FSP bounds [Munsky2006])
- Label: `thm:classical_fsp`
- Given CME generator A and finite set J, if probability mass retained satisfies certain condition, then elementwise bounds hold on truncated solution

**Line 165-245: Remark 2.3** (Stiffness and multiscale challenges)
- Label: `rem:stiffness-challenges`
- Introduces spatial stiffness (connectivity bottlenecks with bridge states) and temporal stiffness (flux variation over time)
- Bottleneck state $s_b$ defined: negligible probability but large exit rate, creates fast pathway between slow metastable regions
- Total flux: $\Phi_{\text{total}}(t) = \sum_x p(x,t) w(x)$ where $w(x) = \sum_k \alpha_k(x)$

**Line 341-350: Remark 3.1** (Total flux versus boundary outflux)
- Label: `rem:total-vs-boundary-flux`
- Explains why total flux $\Phi(x,t) = p(x,t) w(x)$ is preferable to boundary outflux $\Phi_\partial(x,t)$
- Two reasons: (1) bottleneck states have near-zero boundary outflux, (2) computing boundary outflux creates circular dependency

**Line 399-403: Remark 3.2** (Compressed generator construction)
- Algorithm 3.2 directly constructs compressed generator $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}$, not truncated generator
- Renormalization in Algorithm 3.1 compensates for pruned mass, not generator leakage

**Line 547-558: Corollary 4.1** (Truncated generator contraction)
- Label: `cor:truncated-contraction`
- Truncated generator $\mathbf{A}_{JJ}$ generates positive contraction semigroup: $\|e^{t\mathbf{A}_{JJ}}\|_{1\to 1} \leq 1$

**Line 560-562: Remark 4.2** (Infinite-dimensional extension)
- Label: `rem:infinite-dimensional`
- Arguments extend to full CME on infinite state space via Hille-Yosida theorem

**Line 586-612: Theorem 4.3** (Local model error bound)
- Label: `thm:local-model-error`
- Over single time step, local model error: $\|\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}(t_{n+1})\|_1 \leq \int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}} (\Phi_{\text{in}}(s) + \Phi_{\text{out}}(s)) ds$
- Boundary fluxes bounded by sum of influx and outflux

**Line 632-665: Corollary 4.4** (Global error bound)
- Label: `cor:global-error`
- Global error: $e_N \leq \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} (\varepsilon_n + \tau_n)$
- Separates model error from time-stepping error; additive accumulation due to contraction

**Line 670-690: Corollary 4.5** (Combined flux and probability error control)
- Label: `cor:local-error-pruning`
- Local error: $\|\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}(t_{n+1})\|_1 \lesssim (\epsilon_{\text{flux}} \cdot \Phi_{\text{total}}(t_n) + \alpha \cdot w_{\max}) \cdot \Delta t_n$
- Separates contributions from flux-protected states and probability-pruned states
- Key: $w_{\max}$ is computable as byproduct of flux computation in Algorithm 3.1

**Line 694-742: Corollary 4.6** (Adaptive time step)
- Label: `cor:flux-timestep`
- Introduces spatial stiffness ratio: $\kappa_n = \lambda_{\max} / \Phi_{\text{total}} \geq 1$
- Two time-step rules:
  - **(i) Total-flux rule (recommended)**: $\Delta t_n = \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$ with error $\lesssim \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$, expansion factor $\mu_n = \kappa_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$
  - **(ii) Maximum-flux rule (concentrated distributions only)**: $\Delta t_n = \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\max}$ with error $\lesssim \eta_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$ where $\eta_n = \Phi_{\text{total}} / \Phi_{\max}$
- **Caution**: max-flux rule fails for spread distributions (e.g., Oregonator), causing wavefront escape

**Line 744-757: Remark 4.3** (Max-propensity cap and depth-one guarantee)
- Label: `rem:max-propensity-cap`
- To enforce $\mu_n \leq 1$ unconditionally: $\Delta t_n = \min(\varepsilon_{\Delta t}/\Phi_{\text{total}}, 1/\lambda_{\max})$
- Ensures depth-one expansion suffices; when cap activates, error $\lesssim 1/\kappa_n \leq \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$

**Line 760-799: Corollary 4.7** (Expansion depth for boundary control)
- Label: `cor:expansion-depth`
- After expanding by graph depth $d$, outflux satisfied: $\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}} \Phi_{\text{out}}(s) ds \leq \lambda_{\max} \Delta t_n \cdot P(\text{Poisson}(\lambda_{\max} \Delta t_n) \geq d)$
- Minimum depth: $d_{\min} = \lceil \mu + z_\varepsilon \sqrt{\mu} \rceil$ where $\mu = \lambda_{\max} \Delta t_n$
- In terms of stiffness: $d_{\min} = \lceil \kappa_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t} + z_\varepsilon \sqrt{\kappa_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t}} \rceil$

**Line 801-809: Remark 4.4** (Expansion strategy and depth-one regime)
- Label: `rem:expansion-strategy`
- Two strategies: (1) **Stoichiometric expansion** (conservative, adds all R reaction neighbors), (2) **SSA expansion** (samples one direction per state)

**Line 811-825: Remark 4.5** (Consistent parameter selection via spatial stiffness)
- Label: `rem:consistent-params`
- Unified framework governed by spatial stiffness ratio $\kappa = \lambda_{\max} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$
- Parameter guidance for time step, expansion depth, and flux tolerance in terms of $\kappa$ and $\varepsilon_{\Delta t}$
- Bottleneck example: $\kappa \approx 10^5$ early on; max-propensity cap reduces $d_{\min}$ from ~10^5 to 1 while error $1/\kappa \ll \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$

---

### **ALGORITHM DESCRIPTIONS**

**Lines 144-159: Algorithm 1** (FSP with Time Stepping and State Space Control)
- **Label**: `alg:fsp-naive`
- Basic expand-evolve-prune skeleton
- **Steps**: 
  - Initialize: $t \gets t_0$, $J \gets \{x_0\}$, $p \gets [1]$
  - While $t < t_f$:
    - Expand: add neighbors reachable by $r$ reactions
    - Assemble: build $\mathbf{A}_{JJ}$
    - Evolve: $p \gets \exp(\mathbf{A}_{JJ} \Delta t) p$
    - Prune: remove states below heuristic threshold

**Lines 309-337: Algorithm 2** (Flux-Preserving Pruning)
- **Label**: `alg:flux-prune`
- **Three stages**:
  1. **Candidate Selection**: Sort states by probability, identify $\alpha$-quantile as candidates
  2. **Flux-Based Protection**: 
     - Compute exit rate $w(x) = -\mathbf{A}_{xx}$ for each state
     - Compute flux $\Phi(x,t) = p(x,t) \cdot w(x)$
     - Set flux threshold: $\Phi_{\text{thr}} = \epsilon_{\text{flux}} \cdot \Phi_{\text{total}}$
     - Retain states in $\mathcal{C}$ with $\Phi(x,t) \geq \Phi_{\text{thr}}$
  3. **Update and Renormalization**: Remove unprotected candidates, renormalize probability

**Lines 367-395: Algorithm 3** (Forward Enumeration Matrix Construction)
- **Label**: `alg:matrix_construction`
- **Complexity**: $O(|\mathcal{S}| \cdot R)$ where $R$ = number of reactions
- **Method**: For each state $x \in \mathcal{S}$ and reaction $k$:
  - Compute destination $y = x + \nu_k$
  - If $y \in \mathcal{S}$, add propensity to off-diagonal
  - Diagonal = negative sum of off-diagonal entries
- Constructs compressed generator directly with zero column sums

**Lines 409-426: Algorithm 4** (Flux-Adaptive FSP)
- **Label**: `alg:fsp-flux-adaptive`
- **Main loop steps**:
  1. **Expand**: $\mathcal{S}_{\text{new}} \gets \mathcal{S} \cup \partial \mathcal{S}$
  2. **Construct**: Build $\mathbf{A}_{\text{new}}$ via forward enumeration (Algorithm 3)
  3. **Adapt step**: Compute $\Phi_{\text{total}} = \sum_x p(x,t) w(x)$, set $\Delta t = \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$ (Eq. 3.17)
  4. **Evolve**: $p \gets \exp(\mathbf{A}_{\text{new}} \Delta t) p$
  5. **Prune**: Apply flux-preserving pruning (Algorithm 2) with $\alpha, \epsilon_{\text{flux}}$
  6. Update state, probability, generator; advance time

---

### **NUMERICAL EXPERIMENTS** (Section 5)

**5.1 Bottleneck Reaction System** (Lines 866-971)
- **Reactions**: $A \xrightarrow{k_1} B$, $B \xrightarrow{k_2} B + C$
- **Parameters**: $k_1 = 10^{-6}$ s⁻¹, $k_2 = 1$ s⁻¹
- **Key finding**: Intermediate states $(0, 1, C)$ have near-zero probability but large flux
- **Table 1** (Line 886): Shows quasi-bimodal structure; $p(1,0,0)$ transfers to $p(0,1,C_{\max})$ over 3 million seconds
- **Table 2** (Line 903): Probability vs. flux rankings reveal 100-fold disconnect at early times
- **Results with flux-based pruning**: Correctly captures transition; state space grows from 4 to 9000 states
- **Results with probability-only pruning**: Removes all intermediates immediately, creating absorbing state
- **Error analysis** (Figure 6): Relative error decays from 0.1% to 0.015%; absolute error scales linearly: $\epsilon \approx 1.11 \times 10^{-4} \langle C \rangle$ (0.01% relative error)

**5.2 Stochastic Toggle Switch** (Lines 973-1008)
- **Model**: Genetic toggle switch with mutual repression (Hill coefficient $n=3$)
- **Reactions**: 4 reactions with Hill-type kinetics
- **Figure 4**: Shows state space contours at three time points, comparing pruning mass 0.3 vs. 0.001, with/without flux filter

**5.3 Oregonator Model** (Lines 1032-1078)
- **System**: 5 reactions, 3 species (X, Y, Z); characteristic oscillations with three orders of magnitude timescale separation
- **Rate constants**: Determined from steady-state flux balance at $(N_X^*, N_Y^*, N_Z^*) = (500, 1000, 2000)$; $k_3 = 104$ s⁻¹ (fast autocatalysis), $k_1 = 2$ s⁻¹ (slow initiation), $k_2 = 0.1$ molec⁻¹s⁻¹ (fast inhibition)
- **Period**: ~0.85 time units
- **Results**: 
  - Adaptive $\Delta t$ varies 100-fold: $[1.4 \times 10^{-6}, 1.9 \times 10^{-5}]$ s
  - State space: 50-2000 states (compression ratio $\sim 10^8:1$ vs. theoretical $3 \times 10^{11}$ states)
  - Mean trajectories exhibit characteristic relaxation oscillations

**5.4 Robertson Autocatalytic System** (Lines 1080-1117)
- **Reactions**: 3 reactions; $A \to B$, $2B \to B+C$, $B+C \to A+C$
- **Parameters**: $k_1 = 0.04$ s⁻¹, $k_2 = 3 \times 10^7$ molec⁻¹s⁻¹, $k_3 = 10^4$ molec⁻¹s⁻¹
- **Stiffness ratio**: $k_2/k_1 \approx 7.5 \times 10^8$ (nine orders of magnitude)
- **Results over $[10^{-5}, 10^5]$ s**:
  - Three phases: slow initiation ($t < 10^{-2}$), explosive transient ($10^{-2} < t < 10^2$), protracted equilibration ($t > 10^2$)
  - Time step spans 7 orders of magnitude
  - State space: 50 states initially, expands to 2000 during burst, contracts to 500-1000 at equilibration
  - Compression ratio $\sim 10^4:1$ vs. theoretical $3 \times 10^7$ states

**5.5 Matrix Construction Performance** (Lines 1119-1171)
- **Benchmark**: Forward enumeration vs. standard construction on Oregonator, Robertson, Toggle Switch
- **Results on Robertson**:
  - Standard construction: 6.95 ms median (std. dev. 2.33 ms)
  - Forward enumeration: 0.54 ms median (std. dev. 1.12 ms)
  - **Speedup: 12.9x** (Table 7, Line 1135)
- **Total simulation times** (Table 8, Line 1161):
  - Oregonator: 3.9x speedup (4000s → 1093s)
  - Robertson: 3.5x speedup (10421s → 3015s)
  - Toggle switch: 9.8x speedup (364s → 37s)

**5.6 Comparison with Krylov-FSP-SSA** (Lines 1173-1304)

**Oregonator comparison** (Table 6, Lines 1182-1197):
- **Flux-based Adaptive FSP**: 33 s, 26 snapshots, reaches $t=0.11$ (complete), max $|S|=1003$, 0 rejections
- **Krylov-FSP-SSA**: 74 s, 3000 iterations, reaches $t=0.003$ (2.7%), max $|S|=13294$
- **Key difference**: Flux-adaptive time stepping adjusts $\Delta t \in [1.4 \times 10^{-6}, 1.9 \times 10^{-5}]$; Krylov-FSP-SSA locked at $\tau = 10^{-6}$

**Bottleneck comparison** (Table 7, Lines 1213-1228):
- **Flux-based FSP**: 1.0 s, 1000 steps (fixed $\delta t = 10$ s), $\langle C \rangle = 4.978$ (<0.1% error)
- **Krylov-FSP-SSA**: <0.1 s, 7 iterations, $\tau$ grows 100→3700 s, $\langle C \rangle = 0.12$ (40x error)
- **Failure mode**: Wavefront truncation (not connectivity loss); depth-$r=1$ expansion cannot track fast $C$ growth

**Robertson comparison** (Table 8, Lines 1245-1261):
- **Flux-based FSP**: 1117 s, 662,472 steps, reaches $t=10^4$ (complete), $\langle A \rangle=507$, $\langle C \rangle=9493$
- **Krylov-FSP-SSA**: 1.9 s, 500 iterations, 67% rejection rate, reaches only $t=228$ (2.3%)
- **Failure mode**: $\tau$-locked by $k_2=3 \times 10^6$ stiffness via both FSP mass-loss violations and numerical overflow in Krylov exponential

**5.7 Efficiency Under Corrected Krylov-FSP-SSA Parameters** (Lines 1274-1302)
- **Oregonator**: $\tau$-lock is intrinsic to mass-conservation; cannot be resolved
- **Bottleneck**: Parameter tuning achieves at best $\langle C \rangle \approx 4.72$ (5% error) at comparable wall time to Flux-FSP (which achieves <0.1% error)
- **Robertson**: Krylov-FSP-SSA still does not complete $t_f = 10^4$ even with optimized parameters; FP-FSP is only method that succeeds

---

### **DISCUSSION & CONCLUSION** (Lines 1306-1331)

**Discussion** (Lines 1309-1325):
- Flux-based pruning + flux-adaptive time stepping provide complementary robustness advantages
- Fixed $r$-step expansion and constant-in-time $(\alpha, \epsilon_{\text{flux}})$ suffice for test problems
- Method well-suited to mass-conserving systems with bounded dynamically relevant regions
- Hybrid schemes combining flux-based criteria with aggregation methods remain open
- Future directions: tensor-structured methods for higher dimensions, spectral stability guarantees via Dobrushin coefficients, parallelization, time-dependent propensities

**Conclusion** (Lines 1330-1330):
- Flux-based pruning preserves network connectivity on bottleneck systems where probability-only pruning fails
- Flux-adaptive time stepping handles oscillatory systems with time-varying activity
- Additive error accumulation due to contraction properties
- Relative errors ~0.01-0.02% while using state spaces orders of magnitude smaller
- Method successfully handles problems where probability-only pruning severs connector states
- Threshold selection requires problem-specific tuning based on stiffness and timescale separation

---

## **response_round2.tex** — RESPONSE LETTER SUMMARY

**Title**: "Response to Reviewers — Round 2" (Line 15-18)
**Submitted to**: SIAM Multiscale Modeling and Simulation

### **STRUCTURE**

**Response to Referee 1** (Lines 39-84)

**Comment 1.1** (Lines 42-48): Why use total flux instead of boundary outflux for protection?
- **Response**: Two reasons why total flux is preferable:
  1. **Bottleneck states have near-zero boundary outflux** (Lines 55-59): Their transitions lead inside high-probability regions already in $J$; boundary-outflux protection would fail to retain them. Total flux $p(s_b) w(s_b)$ is large because $w(s_b)$ is large, measuring rate probability cycles through $s_b$ regardless of transition destinations.
  2. **Circular dependency** (Lines 61-63): Computing $\Phi_\partial$ requires knowing $J'$, determined by pruning decision itself. Total flux is byproduct of generator diagonal, requires no knowledge of pruning outcome.
- **Action**: Added Remark 3.1 to manuscript making distinction explicit.

**Comment 1.2** (Lines 69-70): Term for flux $w(x)$ used before defined (Line 140)
- **Response**: Added inline definition of $w(x)$ at first use in Remark 2.3, so reader doesn't need to look ahead to Section 3 for formal definition.

**Comment 1.3** (Lines 78-80): Fig. 2 should visualize flux on arrows
- **Response**: TODO note (Line 83) — indicating planned revision to TikZ diagram with flux labels.

**Response to Referee 2** (Lines 86-275)

**Theoretical Issues Subsection** (Lines 89-161)

**Comment 2.1** (Lines 91-94): Notational error in Eq. (4.4) for boundary fluxes
- **Response**: Added explicit clarification of column convention after Eq. (4.4): block $\mathbf{A}_{J'J}$ has rows indexed by $J'$, columns indexed by $J$, so product $\mathbf{A}_{J'J} p_J$ gives rate probability flows OUT of $J$ into $J'$. Notation now consistent throughout Section 4.

**Comment 2.2** (Lines 105-109): Unjustified inequality $\Phi_{\text{in}} + \Phi_{\text{out}} \leq \Phi_{\max}$ in adaptive time-step derivation
- **Response** (Lines 111-120): Replaced with trivially valid bound: $\Phi_{\text{out}} \leq \Phi_{\text{total}}$ (boundary outflux is subset of total flux). Adaptive time-step rule in Corollary 4.7 now reads $\Delta t \leq \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$; proof follows immediately; subsequent corollaries unaffected.

**Comment 2.3** (Lines 124-128): Algorithm performs renormalization after pruning, but theoretical analysis uses compressed generator—relationship unclear; error bounds validity uncertain
- **Response** (Lines 130-160): **No gap between theory and implementation**. Implementation directly constructs compressed generator $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}$, not truncated generator + renormalization. Algorithm 3.2 builds generator column-by-column; off-diagonal entries included only if destination $y \in J$; diagonal set to negative partial column sum. Transitions exiting $J$ excluded from both off-diagonal and diagonal, so column sums exactly zero by construction—the defining property of compressed generator (Proposition 4.1, property 1). Matrix exponential $e^{\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}\Delta t}$ conserves $\mathbf{1}^T p$ exactly.

Renormalization $p \gets p / \|p\|_1$ in Algorithm 3.1 (Stage 3) serves different purpose: compensates for probability mass discarded when low-probability states removed during pruning, not for generator leakage. Pruned mass is at most $\alpha$ by quantile selection (Stage 1). Error analysis formulated in terms of $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}$ applies directly without additional approximation gap. **Added Remark 4.4** to revised manuscript making distinction explicit.

**Comment 2.4** (Lines 164-167): How robustly estimate $w_{\max}$ (maximum exit rate of pruned states) on truncated domain?
- **Response** (Lines 169-176): Exit rate $w(x) = \sum_k \alpha_k(x)$ computed for every state in active set BEFORE pruning (needed for flux computation in Algorithm 3.1, Stage 2). Since pruning only removes subset of current active states, $w_{\max}$ over pruned states available as byproduct with no need to evaluate $w(x)$ outside active set. Corollary 4.7 now states explicitly. **Clarified Corollary 4.5**.

**Empirical Issues Subsection** (Lines 178-276)

**Comment 2.5** (Lines 180-182): Manuscript lacks head-to-head comparison against strong adaptive FSP baselines like ETFSP
- **Response** (Lines 184-213): **Added Section 5.6** providing head-to-head comparison of flux-based adaptive FSP against Krylov-FSP-SSA method of Vo & Sidje (Sidje2015), reviewed by Dinh & Sidje (Dinh2016). This baseline shares same expand-evolve-prune skeleton and Krylov matrix exponential integrator, differing in pruning (joint probability-and-derivative threshold per Algorithm 2 of VoSidje2016, no flux-based protection), time stepping (mass-conservation accept/reject, not flux-adaptive), and expansion (SSA-driven reachability).

Results presented in **Tables 7-9 and Figures 7-8**:
- **Oregonator**: Flux-adaptive FSP completes in 33s, 26 snapshots, max|S|≤1003; Krylov-FSP-SSA reaches t=0.003 (2.7%) after 3000 iters, 74s, |S|=13294. Flux-adaptive time stepping key advantage.
- **Bottleneck**: Both retain B=1; flux-based gets ⟨C⟩=4.978 (reference); Krylov-FSP-SSA gets ⟨C⟩=0.12 (40x below) due to wavefront truncation (τ doubles 100→3700, but depth-1 expansion adds only 1 state/step).

### **THEOREMS, LEMMAS, COROLLARIES, & REMARKS**

**Line 98-105: Remark 2.1** (Generator matrix properties)
- Lists three properties: off-diagonal nonnegative, diagonal nonpositive, column sums zero

**Line 116-130: Theorem 2.2** (Classical FSP bounds [Munsky2006])
- Label: `thm:classical_fsp`
- Given CME generator A and finite set J, if probability mass retained satisfies certain condition, then elementwise bounds hold on truncated solution

**Line 165-245: Remark 2.3** (Stiffness and multiscale challenges)
- Label: `rem:stiffness-challenges`
- Introduces spatial stiffness (connectivity bottlenecks with bridge states) and temporal stiffness (flux variation over time)
- Bottleneck state $s_b$ defined: negligible probability but large exit rate, creates fast pathway between slow metastable regions
- Total flux: $\Phi_{\text{total}}(t) = \sum_x p(x,t) w(x)$ where $w(x) = \sum_k \alpha_k(x)$

**Line 341-350: Remark 3.1** (Total flux versus boundary outflux)
- Label: `rem:total-vs-boundary-flux`
- Explains why total flux $\Phi(x,t) = p(x,t) w(x)$ is preferable to boundary outflux $\Phi_\partial(x,t)$
- Two reasons: (1) bottleneck states have near-zero boundary outflux, (2) computing boundary outflux creates circular dependency

**Line 399-403: Remark 3.2** (Compressed generator construction)
- Algorithm 3.2 directly constructs compressed generator $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}$, not truncated generator
- Renormalization in Algorithm 3.1 compensates for pruned mass, not generator leakage

**Line 547-558: Corollary 4.1** (Truncated generator contraction)
- Label: `cor:truncated-contraction`
- Truncated generator $\mathbf{A}_{JJ}$ generates positive contraction semigroup: $\|e^{t\mathbf{A}_{JJ}}\|_{1\to 1} \leq 1$

**Line 560-562: Remark 4.2** (Infinite-dimensional extension)
- Label: `rem:infinite-dimensional`
- Arguments extend to full CME on infinite state space via Hille-Yosida theorem

**Line 586-612: Theorem 4.3** (Local model error bound)
- Label: `thm:local-model-error`
- Over single time step, local model error: $\|\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}(t_{n+1})\|_1 \leq \int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}} (\Phi_{\text{in}}(s) + \Phi_{\text{out}}(s)) ds$
- Boundary fluxes bounded by sum of influx and outflux

**Line 632-665: Corollary 4.4** (Global error bound)
- Label: `cor:global-error`
- Global error: $e_N \leq \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} (\varepsilon_n + \tau_n)$
- Separates model error from time-stepping error; additive accumulation due to contraction

**Line 670-690: Corollary 4.5** (Combined flux and probability error control)
- Label: `cor:local-error-pruning`
- Local error: $\|\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}(t_{n+1})\|_1 \lesssim (\epsilon_{\text{flux}} \cdot \Phi_{\text{total}}(t_n) + \alpha \cdot w_{\max}) \cdot \Delta t_n$
- Separates contributions from flux-protected states and probability-pruned states
- Key: $w_{\max}$ is computable as byproduct of flux computation in Algorithm 3.1

**Line 694-742: Corollary 4.6** (Adaptive time step)
- Label: `cor:flux-timestep`
- Introduces spatial stiffness ratio: $\kappa_n = \lambda_{\max} / \Phi_{\text{total}} \geq 1$
- Two time-step rules:
  - **(i) Total-flux rule (recommended)**: $\Delta t_n = \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$ with error $\lesssim \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$, expansion factor $\mu_n = \kappa_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$
  - **(ii) Maximum-flux rule (concentrated distributions only)**: $\Delta t_n = \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\max}$ with error $\lesssim \eta_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$ where $\eta_n = \Phi_{\text{total}} / \Phi_{\max}$
- **Caution**: max-flux rule fails for spread distributions (e.g., Oregonator), causing wavefront escape

**Line 744-757: Remark 4.3** (Max-propensity cap and depth-one guarantee)
- Label: `rem:max-propensity-cap`
- To enforce $\mu_n \leq 1$ unconditionally: $\Delta t_n = \min(\varepsilon_{\Delta t}/\Phi_{\text{total}}, 1/\lambda_{\max})$
- Ensures depth-one expansion suffices; when cap activates, error $\lesssim 1/\kappa_n \leq \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$

**Line 760-799: Corollary 4.7** (Expansion depth for boundary control)
- Label: `cor:expansion-depth`
- After expanding by graph depth $d$, outflux satisfied: $\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}} \Phi_{\text{out}}(s) ds \leq \lambda_{\max} \Delta t_n \cdot P(\text{Poisson}(\lambda_{\max} \Delta t_n) \geq d)$
- Minimum depth: $d_{\min} = \lceil \mu + z_\varepsilon \sqrt{\mu} \rceil$ where $\mu = \lambda_{\max} \Delta t_n$
- In terms of stiffness: $d_{\min} = \lceil \kappa_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t} + z_\varepsilon \sqrt{\kappa_n \varepsilon_{\Delta t}} \rceil$

**Line 801-809: Remark 4.4** (Expansion strategy and depth-one regime)
- Label: `rem:expansion-strategy`
- Two strategies: (1) **Stoichiometric expansion** (conservative, adds all R reaction neighbors), (2) **SSA expansion** (samples one direction per state)

**Line 811-825: Remark 4.5** (Consistent parameter selection via spatial stiffness)
- Label: `rem:consistent-params`
- Unified framework governed by spatial stiffness ratio $\kappa = \lambda_{\max} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$
- Parameter guidance for time step, expansion depth, and flux tolerance in terms of $\kappa$ and $\varepsilon_{\Delta t}$
- Bottleneck example: $\kappa \approx 10^5$ early on; max-propensity cap reduces $d_{\min}$ from ~10^5 to 1 while error $1/\kappa \ll \varepsilon_{\Delta t}$

---

### **ALGORITHM DESCRIPTIONS**

**Lines 144-159: Algorithm 1** (FSP with Time Stepping and State Space Control)
- **Label**: `alg:fsp-naive`
- Basic expand-evolve-prune skeleton
- **Steps**: 
  - Initialize: $t \gets t_0$, $J \gets \{x_0\}$, $p \gets [1]$
  - While $t < t_f$:
    - Expand: add neighbors reachable by $r$ reactions
    - Assemble: build $\mathbf{A}_{JJ}$
    - Evolve: $p \gets \exp(\mathbf{A}_{JJ} \Delta t) p$
    - Prune: remove states below heuristic threshold

**Lines 309-337: Algorithm 2** (Flux-Preserving Pruning)
- **Label**: `alg:flux-prune`
- **Three stages**:
  1. **Candidate Selection**: Sort states by probability, identify $\alpha$-quantile as candidates
  2. **Flux-Based Protection**: 
     - Compute exit rate $w(x) = -\mathbf{A}_{xx}$ for each state
     - Compute flux $\Phi(x,t) = p(x,t) \cdot w(x)$
     - Set flux threshold: $\Phi_{\text{thr}} = \epsilon_{\text{flux}} \cdot \Phi_{\text{total}}$
     - Retain states in $\mathcal{C}$ with $\Phi(x,t) \geq \Phi_{\text{thr}}$
  3. **Update and Renormalization**: Remove unprotected candidates, renormalize probability

**Lines 367-395: Algorithm 3** (Forward Enumeration Matrix Construction)
- **Label**: `alg:matrix_construction`
- **Complexity**: $O(|\mathcal{S}| \cdot R)$ where $R$ = number of reactions
- **Method**: For each state $x \in \mathcal{S}$ and reaction $k$:
  - Compute destination $y = x + \nu_k$
  - If $y \in \mathcal{S}$, add propensity to off-diagonal
  - Diagonal = negative sum of off-diagonal entries
- Constructs compressed generator directly with zero column sums

**Lines 409-426: Algorithm 4** (Flux-Adaptive FSP)
- **Label**: `alg:fsp-flux-adaptive`
- **Main loop steps**:
  1. **Expand**: $\mathcal{S}_{\text{new}} \gets \mathcal{S} \cup \partial \mathcal{S}$
  2. **Construct**: Build $\mathbf{A}_{\text{new}}$ via forward enumeration (Algorithm 3)
  3. **Adapt step**: Compute $\Phi_{\text{total}} = \sum_x p(x,t) w(x)$, set $\Delta t = \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$ (Eq. 3.17)
  4. **Evolve**: $p \gets \exp(\mathbf{A}_{\text{new}} \Delta t) p$
  5. **Prune**: Apply flux-preserving pruning (Algorithm 2) with $\alpha, \epsilon_{\text{flux}}$
  6. Update state, probability, generator; advance time

---

### **NUMERICAL EXPERIMENTS** (Section 5)

## **response_round2.tex** — RESPONSE LETTER SUMMARY

**Title**: "Response to Reviewers — Round 2" (Line 15-18)
**Submitted to**: SIAM Multiscale Modeling and Simulation

### **STRUCTURE**

**Response to Referee 1** (Lines 39-84)

**Comment 1.1** (Lines 42-48): Why use total flux instead of boundary outflux for protection?
- **Response**: Two reasons why total flux is preferable:
  1. **Bottleneck states have near-zero boundary outflux** (Lines 55-59): Their transitions lead inside high-probability regions already in $J$; boundary-outflux protection would fail to retain them. Total flux $p(s_b) w(s_b)$ is large because $w(s_b)$ is large, measuring rate probability cycles through $s_b$ regardless of transition destinations.
  2. **Circular dependency** (Lines 61-63): Computing $\Phi_\partial$ requires knowing $J'$, determined by pruning decision itself. Total flux is byproduct of generator diagonal, requires no knowledge of pruning outcome.
- **Action**: Added Remark 3.1 to manuscript making distinction explicit.

**Comment 1.2** (Lines 69-70): Term for flux $w(x)$ used before defined (Line 140)
- **Response**: Added inline definition of $w(x)$ at first use in Remark 2.3, so reader doesn't need to look ahead to Section 3 for formal definition.

**Comment 1.3** (Lines 78-80): Fig. 2 should visualize flux on arrows
- **Response**: TODO note (Line 83) — indicating planned revision to TikZ diagram with flux labels.

**Response to Referee 2** (Lines 86-275)

**Theoretical Issues Subsection** (Lines 89-161)

**Comment 2.1** (Lines 91-94): Notational error in Eq. (4.4) for boundary fluxes
- **Response**: Added explicit clarification of column convention after Eq. (4.4): block $\mathbf{A}_{J'J}$ has rows indexed by $J'$, columns indexed by $J$, so product $\mathbf{A}_{J'J} p_J$ gives rate probability flows OUT of $J$ into $J'$. Notation now consistent throughout Section 4.

**Comment 2.2** (Lines 105-109): Unjustified inequality $\Phi_{\text{in}} + \Phi_{\text{out}} \leq \Phi_{\max}$ in adaptive time-step derivation
- **Response** (Lines 111-120): Replaced with trivially valid bound: $\Phi_{\text{out}} \leq \Phi_{\text{total}}$ (boundary outflux is subset of total flux). Adaptive time-step rule in Corollary 4.7 now reads $\Delta t \leq \varepsilon_{\Delta t} / \Phi_{\text{total}}$; proof follows immediately; subsequent corollaries unaffected.

**Comment 2.3** (Lines 124-128): Algorithm performs renormalization after pruning, but theoretical analysis uses compressed generator—relationship unclear; error bounds validity uncertain
- **Response** (Lines 130-160): **No gap between theory and implementation**. Implementation directly constructs compressed generator $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}$, not truncated generator + renormalization. Algorithm 3.2 builds generator column-by-column; off-diagonal entries included only if destination $y \in J$; diagonal set to negative partial column sum. Transitions exiting $J$ excluded from both off-diagonal and diagonal, so column sums exactly zero by construction—the defining property of compressed generator (Proposition 4.1, property 1). Matrix exponential $e^{\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}\Delta t}$ conserves $\mathbf{1}^T p$ exactly.

Renormalization $p \gets p / \|p\|_1$ in Algorithm 3.1 (Stage 3) serves different purpose: compensates for probability mass discarded when low-probability states removed during pruning, not for generator leakage. Pruned mass is at most $\alpha$ by quantile selection (Stage 1). Error analysis formulated in terms of $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{JJ}$ applies directly without additional approximation gap. **Added Remark 4.4** to revised manuscript making distinction explicit.

**Comment 2.4** (Lines 164-167): How robustly estimate $w_{\max}$ (maximum exit rate of pruned states) on truncated domain?
- **Response** (Lines 169-176): Exit rate $w(x) = \sum_k \alpha_k(x)$ computed for every state in active set BEFORE pruning (needed for flux computation in Algorithm 3.1, Stage 2). Since pruning only removes subset of current active states, $w_{\max}$ over pruned states available as byproduct with no need to evaluate $w(x)$ outside active set. Corollary 4.7 now states explicitly. **Clarified Corollary 4.5**.

**Empirical Issues Subsection** (Lines 178-276)

**Comment 2.5** (Lines 180-182): Manuscript lacks head-to-head comparison against strong adaptive FSP baselines like ETFSP
- **Response** (Lines 184-213): **Added Section 5.6** providing head-to-head comparison of flux-based adaptive FSP against Krylov-FSP-SSA method of Vo & Sidje (Sidje2015), reviewed by Dinh & Sidje (Dinh2016). """
    AdaptiveFSP(; kwargs...)

Algorithm parameters for the adaptive Finite State Projection method.

# Keyword Arguments
- `ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0`: Time-step control numerator.
- `prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1`: Quantile parameter used by pruning.
- `flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6`: Flux protection threshold (relative to total flux).
- `expansion_depth::Int = 1`: Number of neighbor shells added per step.
- `save_interval::Int = 1000`: Save a snapshot every N iterations.
- `max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)`: Maximum number of iterations.
- `flux_method::Symbol = :total`: Time-step denominator: `:total` uses
  `Φ_total = Σᵢ pᵢ·wᵢ` (probability-weighted sum); `:maximum` uses
  `max_i(pᵢ·wᵢ)` (most active state). Use `:maximum` for stiff systems
  where a single high-rate state would otherwise dominate the sum.
- `expand_method::Symbol = :stoich`: State space expansion strategy per step.
  `:stoich` adds all stoichiometric neighbors (`expand!`); `:ssa` adds one
  SSA-sampled successor per state (`expand_ssa!`). Use `:ssa` for oscillatory
  systems (e.g. Oregonator) where `:stoich` inflates the state space.

## Time-step formula

    dt = min(ε_dt / Φ,  tf - t)

where `Φ = Σᵢ pᵢ·wᵢ` (`:total`) or `Φ = maxᵢ pᵢ·wᵢ` (`:maximum`).
"""
Base.@kwdef struct AdaptiveFSP
    ε_dt::Float64 = 1.0
    prob_quantile::Float64 = 0.1
    flux_tolerance::Float64 = 1e-6
    expansion_depth::Int = 1
    save_interval::Int = 1000
    max_iter::Int = typemax(Int)
    flux_method::Symbol = :total
    expand_method::Symbol = :stoich
end

"""
    AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics

Per-step diagnostic data from an AdaptiveFSP solve.

- `dt_log`: time step taken at each iteration.
- `t_log`: simulated time after each iteration.
- `size_log`: projection size `|S|` after each iteration.
- `total_iters`: total number of iterations executed.
"""
struct AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics
    dt_log::Vector{Float64}
    t_log::Vector{Float64}
    size_log::Vector{Int}
    total_iters::Int
end

"""
    solve(prob::FSPProblem, alg::AdaptiveFSP) -> (FSPSolution, AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics)

Run the adaptive FSP algorithm:
1. Expand state space (via `alg.expand_method`: `:stoich` = all neighbors, `:ssa` = SSA-sampled).
2. Build the CME generator (incremental).
3. Compute adaptive time step: `dt = ε_dt / Φ` where `Φ` is total or maximum outflux
   depending on `alg.flux_method`.
4. Propagate probability via matrix exponential (`expv`).
5. Flux-aware pruning + renormalization.
6. Repeat until `t >= tf` or `alg.max_iter` iterations reached.

Returns `(solution, diagnostics)` where `diagnostics` contains per-step
`dt_log`, `t_log`, and `size_log`.
"""
function CommonSolve.solve(prob::FSPProblem{E,T}, alg::AdaptiveFSP) where {E,T}
    model = prob.model
    rates = prob.rates
    bc = prob.bc
    t0, tf = prob.tspan
    n_species = length(Tuple(prob.u0))

    # Initialize state space
    sp = StateSpace{E, Float64}()
    add_state!(sp, prob.u0, 1.0)

    # Solution storage
    sol_t = Float64[t0]
    sol_snaps = [(copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs))]
    sol_sizes = [length(sp)]

    # Per-step diagnostics (lightweight: no state copies)
    dt_log   = Float64[]
    t_log    = Float64[]
    size_log_diag = Int[]

    t = Float64(t0)
    iter = 0

    # Track previous generator for incremental rebuilds
    A_old = spzeros(Float64, 0, 0)
    gids_old = Int[]

    while t < tf && iter < alg.max_iter
        iter += 1

        # 1) Expand state space
        if alg.expand_method === :ssa
            expand_ssa!(sp, model, rates, t, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        else
            expand!(sp, model, bc; depth=alg.expansion_depth)
        end

        # 2) Build generator (incremental rebuild reusing previous matrix)
        A, in_flow, out_flow = reconstruct_generator(sp, model, rates, t, A_old, gids_old)

        # Cache generator state for next iteration's incremental rebuild
        A_old = A
        gids_old = get_global_ids(sp)

        # 3) Adaptive time step
        out_flux = Vector(-out_flow * sp.probs)
        Φ = alg.flux_method === :maximum ? maximum(out_flux) : sum(out_flux)
        dt = Φ > 0 ? alg.ε_dt / Φ : (tf - t)
        dt = min(dt, tf - t)

        # 4) Propagate probability (subcycle if dt*||A||_1 is too large)
            sp.probs = expv(dt, A, sp.probs)

        # 5) Flux-aware pruning + renormalization
        compress!(sp, model, rates, t, alg.prob_quantile;
                  flux_tolerance=alg.flux_tolerance)
        renormalize!(sp)

        # 6) Advance time
        t += dt

        # 7) Record per-step diagnostics
        push!(dt_log, dt)
        push!(t_log, t)
        push!(size_log_diag, length(sp))

        # 8) Save snapshot
        if iter % alg.save_interval == 0 || t >= tf
            push!(sol_t, t)
            push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
            push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
            @info "t = $(round(t; sigdigits=4)), |S| = $(length(sp)), dt = $(round(dt; sigdigits=3))"
        end
    end

    # Ensure final snapshot is captured
    if sol_t[end] < t
        push!(sol_t, t)
        push!(sol_snaps, (copy(sp.states), copy(sp.probs)))
        push!(sol_sizes, length(sp))
    end

    sol  = FSPSolution{E}(sol_t, sol_snaps, sol_sizes, n_species)
    diag = AdaptiveFSPDiagnostics(dt_log, t_log, size_log_diag, iter)
    (sol, diag)
end

# Robertson Autocatalytic System (Extreme Stiffness)
# Saves diagnostics to examples/results/robertson_fpfsp.jls for plotting.
using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Serialization

rn = @reaction_network begin
    k1, A --> B
    k2, 2B --> C + B
    k3, C + B --> A + C
end

rates = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]
prob = FSPProblem(rn, CartesianIndex(10_000, 0, 0), (0.0, 1e4), rates;
                  bounds=(0, 100_001))

t_wall_start = time()
sol, diag = solve(prob, AdaptiveFSP(ε_dt=0.01, prob_quantile=0.4, flux_tolerance=1e-9,
                                    save_interval=1000,
                                    flux_method=:maximum,  # dt = ε_dt / maxᵢ pᵢwᵢ (stiff)
                                    expand_method=:stoich)) # stoichiometric expansion
t_wall = time() - t_wall_start

traj = mean_trajectory(sol)
println("Final: A=$(traj[end,1]), B=$(traj[end,2]), C=$(traj[end,3])")
println("Snapshots: $(length(sol)), final |S| = $(sol.state_space_sizes[end])")
println("Wall time: $(round(t_wall; digits=1))s, total_iters=$(diag.total_iters)")
if !isempty(diag.dt_log)
    println("dt range: $(minimum(diag.dt_log)) to $(maximum(diag.dt_log))")
end

# Save diagnostics for plotting
results_dir = joinpath(@__DIR__, "results")
mkpath(results_dir)
out = Dict(
    "dt_log"      => diag.dt_log,
    "t_log"       => diag.t_log,
    "total_iters" => diag.total_iters,
    "wall_time"   => t_wall,
    "mean_A"      => traj[end, 1],
    "mean_B"      => traj[end, 2],
    "mean_C"      => traj[end, 3],
    "S_final"     => sol.state_space_sizes[end],
)
serialize(joinpath(results_dir, "robertson_fpfsp.jls"), out)
println("Saved diagnostics → examples/results/robertson_fpfsp.jls")

using DiscStochSim, Catalyst, Random

rn = @reaction_network begin
    k1, A --> B

rates = [0.04, 3e6, 1.0]

# AdaptiveFSP
println("Running AdaptiveFSP...")
Random.default_rng(1)

Found it. The critical finding from `test_old_vs_new.jl` (created in commit 1667d30):

The original working Robertson used **`expand_ssa!` + `sum(out_flux)` (total flux)**. The "rober bug fixed" commit changed it to `expand!` (stoich) + `maximum(out_flux)`, which is what's causing the step-lock now.

The reason `:ssa` works: when B is small, SSA picks the dominant reaction A→B (propensity ≈ 400), never adding the 2B→C+B destination states. So the fast k₂ exit rate never gets captured in the generator, and Φ_total stays ≈ k₁·A ≈ small → large dt. With `:stoich`, it immediately adds (9998,1,1) as a neighbor of (9998,2,0), capturing the 3×10⁶ rate and locking dt.

Fix is to revert Robertson to `expand_method=:ssa, flux_method=:total`:
